## Bar / column, side by side

```{r cg-bars-setup, include = FALSE}
## Category labels set in bold, as plotmath, for a summary row or a highlighted bar.
cgb_bold <- function(bold) {
  function(x) parse(text = ifelse(x %in% bold, sprintf("bold(%s)", vapply(x, deparse, "")), vapply(x, deparse, "")))
}
## The black rule at zero that horizontal bars start from when no value is negative.
cgb_zero <- function() geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = lw(0.5))
## The theme for horizontal bars: value axis on top, vertical gridlines, no ticks, no axis rule.
cgb_bars_theme <- function() {
  list(theme_economist(base_size = classic_size, horizontal = FALSE), classic_no_ticks(), classic_no_axis_line())
}
## "77 of 244 panels", or with another name for the panels counted, for a share that reads in running text.
cgb_of <- function(id, unit = NULL) {
  r <- claim(id)
  paste(r$n, "of", r$of, if (is.null(unit)) r$unit else unit)
}
## "69%, 197 of 285 two-series panels".
cgb_share <- function(id, unit = NULL) paste0(pct(id), ", ", cgb_of(id, unit))
## Side-by-side panels with more than one series.
cgb_multi <- claim("type.bar_column_side_by_side")$n - claim("bar_column_side_by_side.series_key.single_series")$n
```

Side-by-side bars are `r pct("type.bar_column_side_by_side")` of panels (`r cgb_of("type.bar_column_side_by_side")`).
Most are horizontal (`r share("bar_column_side_by_side.orientation.horizontal")`), with the value axis on top
(`r share("bar_column_side_by_side.value_axis_side.top")`) and vertical gridlines
(`r share("bar_column_side_by_side.gridlines.vertical")`).
Columns put the axis on the right (`r share("bar_column_side_by_side.value_axis_side.right")`), over horizontal
gridlines.
The cited charts have no ticks and range category labels left:
`r cite_codes(c("20140301_WWC435", "20131102_FNC687", "20140614_CNC156"))`.
Few print values on the bars (`r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.value_labels.some")`).

### One trace

The commonest bar chart has one series (`r share("bar_column_side_by_side.series_key.single_series")`).
A single series is dark blue (`r cgb_share("colour.n1.set.dark blue", "one-series panels of all types")`).
Years are truncated as on line charts
(`r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.truncated_years", "side-by-side panels")`), under a black baseline in the cited
columns: `r cite("bar_column_side_by_side.truncated_years")`.

```{r cg-bars-african-lion, econ_height = 165}
cgb_lion <- data.frame(
  year = 2004:2015,
  growth = c(11.7, 12.7, 11.5, 11.8, 11.2, 10.0, 10.6, 11.4, 8.7, 9.8, 10.3, 8.7)
)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_lion, aes(year, growth)) +
  geom_col(fill = economist_pal()(1), width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 14), breaks = seq(0, 14, 2), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    ## 2014 goes unlabelled so that "15*" has room.
    breaks = c(seq(2004, 2012, 2), 2015), labels = c("2004", "06", "08", "10", "12", "15*"),
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "African lion",
    subtitle = "Ethiopia’s GDP, % change on a year earlier",
    caption = "*Estimate\nSource: IMF",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: dark blue, not mid-blue; no ticks; and a black baseline.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#one-trace))

### One trace with highlight

Horizontal bars start from a black rule at zero: `r cite_codes(c("20140301_WWC435", "20150718_USC083"))`.
To single out a category, bold its label and leave the bar in the series color, as China is in
`r cite_codes("20140405_CNC682")`.
Highlights were not counted. In the highlighted bar charts examined, none recolors a bar; they draw a dashed red
reference line named in red italic capitals, as in "Taxing wages" (April 2014) and `r cite_codes("20150718_USC083")`.

```{r cg-bars-salud, econ_height = 165}
cgb_doctors <- data.frame(
  country = c("Sweden", "Denmark", "Britain", "Portugal", "Luxembourg", "France", "Austria", "Spain", "Germany"),
  visits = c(2.9, 4.6, 5.0, 5.7, 6.3, 6.9, 6.9, 7.5, 8.2)
)
cgb_doctors$country <- factor(cgb_doctors$country, levels = cgb_doctors$country)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_doctors, aes(country, visits)) +
  geom_col(fill = economist_pal()(1), width = 0.6) +
  cgb_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 8.4), breaks = seq(0, 8, 2), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = cgb_bold("Spain")) +
  labs(
    title = "Salud",
    subtitle = "Doctors’ consultations per person\nSelected countries, 2009",
    caption = "Source: OECD",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: the axis on top, a black rule at zero, and Spain marked only by its bold label, where 2017 also colors
its bar a second blue. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#one-trace-with-highlight))

### Two traces

Two series are most often blue and dark blue
(`r cgb_share("colour.n2.set.blue+dark blue", "two-series panels of all types")`), blue first
(`r cgb_share("colour.bar.n2.first.blue", "two-series bar panels")`).
Of the `r cgb_multi` multi-series side-by-side panels, `r claim("bar_column_side_by_side.series_key.legend")$n` have
a legend, `r claim("bar_column_side_by_side.legend.under_subtitle")$n` under the subtitle.
In the cited charts the bars of a pair touch, first series on top:
`r cite_codes(c("20120317_LDC770", "20140405_CNC682", "20131102_FNC687"))`.

```{r cg-bars-defenders, econ_height = 235}
cgb_elections <- data.frame(
  country = rep(
    c("Chile", "Brazil", "Mexico", "Malaysia", "South Africa", "Poland", "India", "Egypt", "Russia"),
    each = 2
  ),
  income = rep(c("Middle class", "Low income"), 9),
  pct = c(80, 66, 69, 62, 64, 55, 61, 52, 59, 49, 54, 44, 53, 51, 51, 48, 51, 37)
)
cgb_elections$country <- factor(cgb_elections$country, levels = rev(unique(cgb_elections$country)))
cgb_elections$income <- factor(cgb_elections$income, levels = c("Middle class", "Low income"))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_elections, aes(country, pct, fill = income)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  cgb_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 80), breaks = seq(0, 80, 20), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "Defenders of democracy",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Respondents saying that honest elections",
      "held regularly with a choice of at least two",
      "political parties are very important,",
      "2007, %",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    caption = "Source: Pew Global Attitudes Survey",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: blue and dark blue, not two blues; the axis on top; and no gap within a pair.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#two-traces))

### Two traces with sub-categories

Grouped bars were not counted. Here each country is a panel named at its top left; the years label the bars, and a
legend under the subtitle keys the forecasts.

```{r cg-bars-autumn-fall, econ_height = 185}
cgb_forecasts <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("Germany", "France", "Euro area", "Spain", "Italy"), each = 4),
  vintage = rep(rep(c("2011", "2012"), each = 2), 5),
  made_in = rep(c("June", "September"), 10),
  gdp = c(3.2, 2.7, 2.0, 1.3, 2.1, 1.7, 1.9, 1.4, 2.0, 1.6, 1.7, 1.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1.6, 1.1, 1.0, 0.6, 1.3, 0.3)
)
cgb_forecasts$country <- factor(cgb_forecasts$country, levels = unique(cgb_forecasts$country))
cgb_forecasts$vintage <- factor(cgb_forecasts$vintage, levels = c("2012", "2011"))
cgb_forecasts$made_in <- factor(cgb_forecasts$made_in, levels = c("June", "September"))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_forecasts, aes(vintage, gdp, fill = made_in)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  cgb_zero() +
  coord_flip() +
  ## Each country is a panel, named at its top left; the years are the bars' own labels.
  facet_grid(rows = vars(.data$country), scales = "free_y", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 3.4), breaks = 0:3, expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "Autumn fall",
    subtitle = "GDP, % increase on previous year",
    caption = "Source: IMF",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Forecasts made in:"
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme() +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = rel(1), margin = margin(r = classic_size, unit = "pt")
    ),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(classic_size * 0.6, "pt")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title.position = "top"))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: blue and dark blue forecasts, and space between countries rather than rules.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#two-traces-with-sub-categories))

Four series take blue-gray, dark blue, blue and gray
(`r cgb_share("colour.n4.set.blue+blue-gray+dark blue+gray", "four-series panels")`), most often blue-gray first
(`r share("colour.bar.n4.first.blue-gray")`): `r cite("colour.n4.set.blue+blue-gray+dark blue+gray", k = 2)`.
"Other" is usually gray, but most gray series are ordinary categories (`r share("colour.gray.equal")`).

```{r cg-bars-mighty-jungle, econ_height = 155}
cgb_returns <- data.frame(
  horizon = rep(c("20 years", "10 years", "5 years"), each = 4),
  asset = rep(c("Equities", "All property", "Rural property", "Forestry"), 3),
  pct = c(7.1, 8.7, 12.5, 9.5, 6.7, 6.1, 11.8, 18.8, 7.7, 10.9, 11.3, 21.1)
)
cgb_returns$horizon <- factor(cgb_returns$horizon, levels = c("20 years", "10 years", "5 years"))
cgb_returns$asset <- factor(cgb_returns$asset, levels = c("Equities", "All property", "Rural property", "Forestry"))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_returns, aes(horizon, pct, fill = asset)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 25), breaks = seq(0, 25, 5), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "The mighty jungle",
    subtitle = "Britain, annualised rate of return\non investment*, %",
    caption = "*To 2014\nSources: MSCI; JP Morgan",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: the classic four colors, gray last, instead of blues and cyans; and a black baseline.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#two-traces-with-sub-categories))

### One trace with a +/- axis

Bars with negative values use an unsigned axis with "– 0 +" at zero
(`r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.negative_labels.plus_minus_at_zero")`):
`r cite("bar_column_side_by_side.negative_labels.plus_minus_at_zero")`.
A red zero line is on `r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.red_zero_line", "side-by-side panels")`.
A summary row is bold, as "Global" is in `r cite_codes("20140222_INC395")`.

```{r cg-bars-dotcom, econ_height = 195}
cgb_capex <- data.frame(
  sector = c(
    "Internet", "Software", "Tech hardware", "IT services", "Health care", "Total", "Leisure", "Chemicals",
    "Oil, gas and fuels", "Metals and mining", "Property", "Energy equipment"
  ),
  change = c(52, 36, 26, 22, 9, -17, -19, -23, -32, -34, -35, -53)
)
cgb_capex$sector <- factor(cgb_capex$sector, levels = rev(cgb_capex$sector))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_capex, aes(sector, change)) +
  geom_col(fill = economist_pal()(1), width = 0.6) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", limits = c(-60, 60), breaks = seq(-60, 60, 20), expand = expansion(0),
    labels = economist_plus_minus_format("horizontal")
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = cgb_bold("Total")) +
  labs(
    title = "Another dotcom boom",
    subtitle = "Change in worldwide capital spending*, %\n2014-17 forecast",
    caption = "*In dollar terms\nSource: Goldman Sachs",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: the axis reads "60 40 20 – 0 + 20 40 60" across the top, where 2017 signs the negative labels along the
bottom. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#one-trace-with-a---axis))

In the cited charts, columns put "+" above zero and "–" below, and keep one color on both sides:
`r cite_codes(c("20130223_ASC106", "20151031_WWC338"))`.
A +/- axis is on `r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.plus_minus_axis", "side-by-side panels")`
(`r pct("bar_column_side_by_side.plus_minus_axis")`), a few with no negative values.

```{r cg-bars-money-drain, econ_height = 155}
## 2005 is missing from the 2017 guide's chart.
cgb_capital <- data.frame(
  year = c(1994:2004, 2006:2011),
  flow = c(-14, -4, -24, -18.5, -22, -21, -25, -15, -8, -1.5, -8, 42, 82, -134, -57, -34, -31.5)
)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_capital, aes(year, flow)) +
  geom_col(fill = economist_pal()(1), width = 0.68) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", limits = c(-150, 100), breaks = seq(-150, 100, 50), expand = expansion(0),
    labels = economist_plus_minus_format()
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1994, 1998, 2002, 2006, 2011), labels = c("1994", "98", "2002", "06", "11*"),
    ## Room on the left, so that "1994" stays inside the chart's margin.
    expand = expansion(add = c(1.1, 0.5))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The money drain",
    subtitle = "Net private capital inflows/outflows, $bn",
    caption = "*To June 30th\nSource: Central Bank of Russia",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: inflows and outflows share dark blue, where 2017 colors them apart; the axis is unsigned, "+ 0 –" at
zero. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#one-trace-with-a---axis))

When the sign means two things, as with exports and imports, the series can take blue and dark red
(`r cgb_share("colour.n2.set.blue+dark red", "two-series panels")`).
The cited charts with this pair have double scales, with axis titles in the series' colors, as in
`r cite_codes("20130427_WBC404")`. This redraw has one scale, so a legend under the subtitle keys the pair.

```{r cg-bars-trader-woes, econ_height = 215}
cgb_trade <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1995:2016, 4),
  country = rep(c("China, as % of GDP", "United States, as % of GDP"), each = 44),
  flow = rep(rep(c("Exports", "Imports"), each = 22), 2),
  pct = c(
    6.2, 5.9, 6.5, 6.9, 7.5, 8.2, 7.6, 8.5, 9.1, 10.0, 10.5,
    10.4, 9.0, 7.3, 5.8, 6.0, 5.3, 5.0, 4.7, 4.4, 4.3, 4.1,
    -1.5, -1.4, -1.2, -1.3, -1.2, -1.3, -1.4, -1.5, -1.7, -1.8, -1.7,
    -1.9, -1.8, -1.4, -1.4, -1.4, -1.3, -1.2, -1.2, -1.1, -0.95, -0.95,
    0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.15, 0.15, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35,
    0.4, 0.5, 0.55, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.7, 0.75, 0.75, 0.7, 0.7,
    -0.7, -0.75, -0.8, -0.9, -0.9, -1.1, -1.1, -1.2, -1.4,
    -1.6, -1.9, -2.1, -2.2, -2.3, -2.1, -2.5, -2.7, -2.7,
    -2.7, -2.75, -2.8, -2.6
  )
)
cgb_trade$country <- factor(cgb_trade$country, levels = c("China, as % of GDP", "United States, as % of GDP"))
cgb_trade$flow <- factor(cgb_trade$flow, levels = c("Exports", "Imports"))
## The two panels' ranges, so that each has its own scale.
cgb_trade_range <- data.frame(
  year = 1995, pct = c(-4, 12, -4, 4),
  country = factor(rep(levels(cgb_trade$country), each = 2), levels = levels(cgb_trade$country))
)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_trade, aes(year, pct, fill = flow)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68) +
  geom_blank(data = cgb_trade_range, aes(year, pct), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  facet_wrap(~country, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", breaks = seq(-4, 12, 4), expand = expansion(0), labels = economist_plus_minus_format()
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2016), labels = c("1995", "2000", "05", "10", "16*"),
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Exports = fg[["blue"]], Imports = fg[["dark red"]])) +
  labs(
    title = "Trader woes",
    subtitle = "China-United States trade in goods",
    caption = "*Jan-Nov annualised\nSources: Census Bureau; IMF",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1)), panel.spacing.y = unit(classic_size * 2.2, "pt"))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: blue and dark red keyed by a legend under the subtitle, where 2017 names the series in the first panel in
their bar colors. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#one-trace-with-a---axis))

### Color overrides

In the cited chart, three quarters in time order take blue-gray, dark blue, then blue, the palette's order:
`r cite_codes("20140222_INC395")`. Blue-gray is the commonest first color of a three-series bar chart
(`r share("colour.bar.n3.first.blue-gray")`). Light-to-dark ramps were not counted.

```{r cg-bars-growth-asia, econ_height = 225}
cgb_asia <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("India", "Cambodia", "Laos", "China", "Malaysia", "Thailand", "Singapore", "Brunei"), each = 3),
  period = rep(c("2015", "2016", "2016-20*"), 8),
  growth = c(7.2, 7.3, 7.3, 7.0, 7.1, 7.3, 6.9, 7.0, 7.3, 6.8, 6.5, 6.0,
             4.6, 4.6, 5.0, 2.7, 3.1, 3.6, 2.1, 2.4, 2.6, -1.4, 0.5, 1.8)
)
cgb_asia$country <- factor(cgb_asia$country, levels = rev(unique(cgb_asia$country)))
cgb_asia$period <- factor(cgb_asia$period, levels = c("2015", "2016", "2016-20*"))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_asia, aes(country, growth, fill = period)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", limits = c(-2, 8), breaks = seq(-2, 8, 2), expand = expansion(0),
    labels = economist_plus_minus_format("horizontal")
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "Growth in Asia",
    subtitle = "GDP forecasts, % change on a year earlier",
    caption = "*Annual average\nSource: OECD",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: blue-gray, dark blue and blue in palette order, not a light-to-dark ramp; and a +/- axis on top.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#color-overrides))

Groups of series take a color family each, blues for one and reds for the other
(`r cgb_of("colour.n4.set.blue+dark blue+dark red+pink", "four-series panels")`):
`r cite("colour.n4.set.blue+dark blue+dark red+pink", k = 2)`.

```{r cg-bars-dont-fence, econ_height = 235}
cgb_segregation <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("White British", "Other White", "Mixed", "Bangladeshi", "Pakistani", "Indian", "Chinese", "African",
                "Caribbean"), each = 4),
  area = rep(c("Inner London", "Outer London", "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities"), 9),
  change = c(
    3.0, 1.7, 1.6, 0.4, -2.7, -0.7, -1.7, 0, -6.3, -8.3, -10.4, -9.3,
    -0.1, -11.8, -3.7, -3.1, -1.0, -4.6, -3.0, -5.3, 0, -1.5, -5.3, -5.2,
    -6.1, -11.5, -11.9, -10.2, 0.3, -3.8, -14.8, -19.9, 1.3, -4.8, -4.7, -7.1
  )
)
cgb_segregation$group <- factor(cgb_segregation$group, levels = rev(unique(cgb_segregation$group)))
cgb_segregation$area <- factor(cgb_segregation$area, levels = c(
  "Inner London", "Outer London", "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities"
))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_segregation, aes(group, change, fill = area)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.84, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.84) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", limits = c(-20, 5), breaks = seq(-20, 5, 5), expand = expansion(0),
    labels = economist_plus_minus_format("horizontal")
  ) +
  ## Dark blue and blue for London, dark red and pink for the other cities.
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(fg[c("dark blue", "blue", "dark red", "pink")])) +
  labs(
    title = "Don’t fence me in",
    subtitle = "Britain, % change in segregation index*\n2001-11",
    caption = "* % that needs to move to create\nan even distribution\nSource: University of Manchester",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme() +
  ## The key reads down its columns, one group to a column.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: the classic blues and reds in place of 2017's, and the +/- axis on top.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#color-overrides))

## Bar / column, stacked

Stacked bars are `r pct("type.bar_column_stacked")` of panels (`r cgb_of("type.bar_column_stacked")`), slightly
more often columns (`r share("bar_column_stacked.orientation.vertical")`).
A legend under the subtitle keys them (`r share("bar_column_stacked.legend.under_subtitle")`):
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.legend.under_subtitle")`.
It was the commonest key every year, though less so after 2012 (`r by_year("bar_column_stacked.legend")`).
In the cited charts, segments meet with no white rule:
`r cite_codes(c("20151003_LDC072", "20130629_INC873", "20120811_LDC772"))`.
Two-series stacks are most often blue and dark blue, in either order (`r cgb_of("colour.n2.stack.blue>dark blue")`
start with blue, `r claim("colour.n2.stack.dark blue>blue")$n` with dark blue).

In `r cgb_of("bar_column_stacked.value_labels.all", "stacked panels")`, every segment carries its value, centered, in
white (black on the palest).
These charts drop the value axis (`r share("bar_column_stacked.value_axis_side.none")`) and name each bar above it:
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.value_labels.all", k = 2)`.

```{r cg-bars-fed-nuptials, econ_height = 149}
cgb_carriers <- data.frame(
  band = rep(c("All mobiles", "Smartphones"), each = 5),
  carrier = rep(c("AT&T", "T-Mobile", "Sprint Nextel", "Verizon", "Other"), 2),
  share = c(30.4, 10.0, 31.4, 11.1, 16.8, 44.1, 9.6, 30.5, 12.9, 8.0),
  ## Segment widths as drawn in the 2017 guide, which differ from its printed values (the smartphone shares sum to
  ## 105.1); the values printed are the shares.
  width = c(26.5, 10.1, 31.5, 11.0, 20.9, 35.1, 12.2, 29.6, 14.8, 8.3)
)
cgb_carriers$carrier <- factor(cgb_carriers$carrier, levels = unique(cgb_carriers$carrier))
cgb_carriers$band <- factor(cgb_carriers$band, levels = c("Smartphones", "All mobiles"))
cgb_bands <- data.frame(band = levels(cgb_carriers$band), row = 1:2)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_carriers, aes(band, width, fill = carrier)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", share), colour = carrier %in% c("Verizon", "Other"), group = carrier),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), size = classic_size / .pt, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ## White on the dark segments, black on the light blue and the gray.
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "white", `TRUE` = "black")) +
  ## Each bar is named above it, ranged left, in place of axis labels.
  geom_text(
    data = cgb_bands, aes(x = row + 0.29, y = 0, label = band), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, vjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = classic_size / .pt
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.5))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(0)) +
  ## Four series in the classic set, "other" in gray and last.
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(c(fg[c("blue-gray", "dark blue", "blue", "light blue")], fg[["gray"]]))) +
  labs(
    title = "The Fed says no to nuptials",
    subtitle = "Mobile operators' US market share\nJuly 2011, %",
    caption = "Source: comScore",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size, horizontal = FALSE) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: centered values, not at the left edge, and the key in stack order with "other" last, not alphabetical.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#bar-column-stacked))
As in the 2017 guide, the segments follow its drawn widths, not the printed shares (the smartphone shares sum to
105.1).

Wide segments are named in place and the rest keyed by the legend:
`r cgb_of("bar_column_stacked.series_key.mixed", "stacked panels")` use this mixed key.
Labeled value lines are on `r cgb_of("bar_column_side_by_side.value_lines.labelled", "side-by-side panels")`. In the
cited chart the line is dashed red and named in red italic capitals: `r cite_codes("20150718_USC083")`.
The party colors are this redraw's choice: greens and light blue for regional parties, reds and blues for national
ones, gray for the rest.

```{r cg-bars-no-winner, econ_height = 129}
cgb_seats <- data.frame(
  party = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Podemos", "PSOE", "Ciudadanos", "PP", "Others"),
  n = c(9, 8, 6, 69, 90, 40, 123, 5)
)
cgb_seats$party <- factor(cgb_seats$party, levels = cgb_seats$party)
## The three biggest parties are named in their segments, the rest in the key.
cgb_seats$label <- ifelse(cgb_seats$n >= 60, paste0(cgb_seats$party, "\n", cgb_seats$n), "")
cgb_majority <- 176

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_seats, aes(1, n, fill = party)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.45, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label, colour = party == "Podemos", group = party),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
    size = classic_size / .pt, lineheight = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ## White on the dark segments, black on the pink.
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "white", `TRUE` = "black")) +
  annotate(
    "segment", x = 0.7, xend = 1.36, y = cgb_majority, yend = cgb_majority, colour = econ_red, linewidth = lw(0.5),
    linetype = "22"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 1.39, y = cgb_majority, label = "176 REQUIRED FOR MAJORITY", colour = econ_red, fontface = "italic",
    vjust = 0, size = classic_size * 0.9 / .pt
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.7, 1.52), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 350), expand = expansion(0)) +
  ## Regional parties in greens and light blue, the national parties in reds and blues, others in gray.
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = setNames(
      unname(fg[c("light green", "dark green", "light blue", "pink", "dark red", "blue", "dark blue", "gray")]),
      levels(cgb_seats$party)
    ),
    breaks = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Ciudadanos", "Others")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "No one's a winner",
    subtitle = "Spanish general election 2015, Seats won",
    caption = "Sources: Ministry of the Interior; El País",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size, horizontal = FALSE) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: no value axis; a dashed red majority line, not a tick on a hand-drawn axis; a legend for the small
parties instead of leader lines; and "Others" at the end of the bar.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#bar-column-stacked))

Stacked bars with different totals were not counted. Here each bar gets a panel and heading. Spending is drawn to
Deir al-Zor's scale, shown only under the Deir al-Zor heading; the much larger overall revenue has its own.
Segments too narrow for a name are labeled above and below the bar on leader lines
(`r cgb_of("bar_column_stacked.leader_lines", "stacked panels")` have them):
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.leader_lines", k = 2)`.

```{r cg-bars-looting, econ_height = 189}
cgb_streams <- c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity")
cgb_spend <- c("Fighters' salary", "Military camps", "Social services", "Islamic police", "Treasury", "Media")
cgb_panels <- c("Overall, monthly revenue $79.8m", "Deir al-Zor governorate, monthly revenue $8.7m", "Monthly spending, $5.8m")
cgb_loot <- data.frame(
  panel = factor(rep(cgb_panels, c(4, 4, 6)), levels = cgb_panels),
  stream = factor(c(cgb_streams, cgb_streams, cgb_spend), levels = c(cgb_streams, cgb_spend)),
  value = c(20.1, 14.3, 12.0, 4.0, 2.3, 3.8, 1.9, 0.4, 2.5, 1.15, 1.0, 0.6, 0.35, 0.2)
)
## The spending bar's first segment is named inside it; the others are named on leader lines from their middles, two
## rows above the bar and two below, each name ending at its line.
cgb_spending <- subset(cgb_loot, panel == cgb_panels[3])
cgb_spending$mid <- cumsum(cgb_spending$value) - cgb_spending$value / 2
cgb_spending$y <- c(1, 1.62, 0.38, -0.2, 1.62, 2.2)
cgb_leaders <- cgb_spending[-1, ]
## Deir al-Zor and spending share one scale, so their bars compare; spending is read against Deir al-Zor's axis and
## has neither labels nor gridlines. facet_wrap() draws an axis on every free panel or on none, so the labels and
## gridlines are drawn as data, above the first two bars.
cgb_shared <- max(tapply(cgb_loot$value, cgb_loot$panel, sum)[cgb_panels[2:3]])
cgb_axis <- data.frame(
  panel = factor(rep(cgb_panels[1:2], c(6, 5)), levels = cgb_panels),
  value = c(seq(0, 50, 10), seq(0, 8, 2))
)
## The panels' heights follow their y ranges: the first two have room above their bars for the labels, the spending
## panel room under its bar for the names.
cgb_room <- data.frame(
  panel = factor(cgb_panels, levels = cgb_panels), value = c(0, 0, cgb_shared), y = c(0.68, 0.68, -0.45),
  y2 = c(1.75, 1.75, 2.45)
)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_loot, aes(value, 1, fill = stream)) +
  geom_segment(
    data = cgb_axis, aes(x = value, xend = value, y = 0.68, yend = 1.4), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.244
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = cgb_axis, aes(x = value, y = 1.45, label = value), inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 0,
    size = classic_size / .pt
  ) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, orientation = "y", position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_blank(data = cgb_room, aes(value, y), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_blank(data = cgb_room, aes(value, y2), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(
    data = cgb_leaders, aes(x = mid, xend = mid, y = ifelse(y > 1, 1.3, 0.7), yend = y), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = lw(0.3)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = cgb_leaders, aes(x = mid, y = y, label = stream), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -0.06,
    size = classic_size * 0.9 / .pt
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = cgb_spending[1, ], aes(x = mid, y = 1, label = stream), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "white",
    size = classic_size * 0.9 / .pt
  ) +
  ## coord_flip() cannot take free scales, so the bars lie along x.
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free", space = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  ## Revenue in the four-series set, spending in the palette's reds, greens and brown.
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = setNames(
      unname(fg[c(
        "blue-gray", "dark blue", "blue", "light blue",
        "dark red", "pink", "brown", "coral", "dark green", "light green"
      )]),
      c(cgb_streams, cgb_spend)
    ),
    breaks = cgb_streams
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Looting the Levant",
    subtitle = "Islamic State's finances*, January 2015, $m",
    caption = "*Estimates\nSource: IHS",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size, horizontal = FALSE) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    ## The heading above the panel's own axis.
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1), face = "bold", margin = margin(b = classic_size * 0.3, unit = "pt")),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(classic_size * 0.5, "pt")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: axes under the overall and Deir al-Zor headings, the spending bar on Deir al-Zor's scale, and the
revenue key under the subtitle. 2017 draws one axis, for the middle bar, and prints the first bar's values. ([2017
version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#bar-column-stacked))
As in the 2017 guide, the segments fall short of the heading totals ($50.4m of $79.8m, $8.4m of $8.7m).

A forecast is a neutral band, the ground darkened, named in italic capitals at its top
(`r share("bar_column_stacked.highlight_regions.labelled neutral")`):
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.highlight_regions.labelled neutral", k = 2)`.
The commonest order of a three-series stack, from the baseline, is blue-gray, dark blue, blue
(`r share("colour.n3.stack.blue-gray>dark blue>blue")`).
Of the `r claim("type.bar_column_stacked")$n` stacked panels, `r claim("bar_column_stacked.value_axis_side.right")$n`
put the value axis on the right and `r claim("bar_column_stacked.truncated_years")$n` truncate the years.

```{r cg-bars-getting-sociable, econ_height = 178}
cgb_adspend <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2008:2017, each = 4),
  format = rep(c("Paid search", "Display", "Classified", "Online video"), 10),
  bn = c(
    24, 15, 9, 4, 27, 16, 9, 4, 32, 19, 9, 6, 37, 19, 10, 10,
    43, 21, 11, 15, 48, 25, 11, 20, 56, 27, 13, 27, 62, 31, 15, 36,
    72, 33, 16, 44, 79, 35, 17, 54
  )
)
cgb_adspend$format <- factor(cgb_adspend$format, levels = unique(cgb_adspend$format))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_adspend, aes(year, bn, fill = format)) +
  classic_band(2014.5, 2017.5, "FORECAST") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 250), breaks = seq(0, 250, 50), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2008:2017, labels = classic_years, expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.5))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(fg[c("blue-gray", "dark blue", "blue", "light blue")])) +
  labs(
    title = "Getting sociable",
    subtitle = "Global internet-advertising spending, $bn",
    caption = "Source: ZenithOptimedia",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  ## Every year is labelled, as in the paper's charts; the sans type is wider than the paper's, so the years are set a
  ## little smaller to keep "2008" and "09" apart.
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.85))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: a full-height forecast band named inside, with no rule over it, and the key under the subtitle, not in
the panel. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#bar-column-stacked))

Stacks below zero are rare (`r claim("bar_column_stacked.negative_labels.plus_minus_at_zero")$of` panels), and
`r claim("bar_column_stacked.negative_labels.plus_minus_at_zero")$n` of them use the +/- axis.
A red zero line is on `r cgb_of("bar_column_stacked.red_zero_line", "stacked panels")`, not all with negative values:
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.red_zero_line", k = 1)`.

```{r cg-bars-more-in-out, econ_height = 179}
cgb_china <- c(
  0.15, 0.18, 0.26, 0.29, 0.37, 0.40, 0.46, 0.55, 0.61, 0.68, 0.79, 0.75, 0.92, 1.05,
  1.30, 1.52, 1.67, 1.76, 1.80, 1.54, 1.80, 1.87, 1.93, 1.89, 1.96, 2.02, 1.83
)
cgb_total <- c(
  1.67, 1.05, 1.27, 1.65, 2.04, 2.06, 2.07, 2.07, 2.50, 3.38, 4.22, 3.85, 4.24, 4.61,
  5.32, 5.89, 5.96, 5.58, 5.52, 3.47, 4.22, 4.66, 4.50, 4.11, 4.20, 4.11, 3.87
)
cgb_deficit <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1990:2016, 2),
  region = rep(c("China", "Rest of world"), each = 27),
  pct = c(-cgb_china, -(cgb_total - cgb_china))
)
cgb_deficit$region <- factor(cgb_deficit$region, levels = c("China", "Rest of world"))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_deficit, aes(year, pct, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  classic_zero_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right", limits = c(-6, 0.6), breaks = seq(-6, 0, 2), expand = expansion(0),
    labels = economist_plus_minus_format()
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2016), labels = c("1990", "95", "2000", "05", "10", "16*"),
    ## Room on the left, so that "1990" stays inside the chart's margin.
    expand = expansion(add = c(1.3, 0.5))
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "More in than out",
    subtitle = "United States, merchandise-trade deficit\n% of GDP",
    caption = "*January-September\nSources: US Census Bureau;\nUS Bureau of Economic Analysis",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist(base_size = classic_size) +
  classic_no_ticks() +
  classic_no_axis_line()

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: an unsigned axis with "+ 0 –" at zero in place of signed labels, and blue and dark blue.
([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#bar-column-stacked))

### Color overrides

Beyond four series the palette adds light blue, then greens. The commonest six-series set is blue, blue-gray, dark
blue, gray, light blue and light green
(`r share("colour.n6.set.blue+blue-gray+dark blue+gray+light blue+light green")`).
This chart needs seven colors, so it takes `economist_pal()(7)`, which adds dark green and keeps gray for "other".
"Other" is gray in `r cgb_of("colour.other.gray", '"other" series')` and last in
`r cgb_of("colour.other.position.last", 'panels with one')`: `r cite("bar_column_stacked.grey_other", k = 2)`.

```{r cg-bars-movers-shakers, econ_height = 179}
cgb_origins <- c("Romania", "Poland", "Italy", "Portugal", "Germany", "Britain")
cgb_shares <- rbind(
  `EU-28` = c(20, 15, 9, 7.5, 5, 0),
  Switzerland = c(0, 0, 20.5, 21, 24, 0),
  Germany = c(5.5, 17.5, 18.5, 0, 0, 0),
  Spain = c(46.5, 0, 9.5, 6, 0, 8),
  France = c(0, 0, 7.5, 42, 0, 8),
  Italy = c(76, 7.5, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  Britain = c(5.5, 29.5, 0, 5.5, 0, 0)
)
cgb_migrants <- data.frame(
  destination = rep(rownames(cgb_shares), times = ncol(cgb_shares) + 1),
  origin = rep(c(cgb_origins, "Other"), each = nrow(cgb_shares)),
  pct = c(cgb_shares, 100 - rowSums(cgb_shares))
)
cgb_migrants$origin <- factor(cgb_migrants$origin, levels = c(cgb_origins, "Other"))
cgb_migrants$destination <- factor(cgb_migrants$destination, levels = rev(rownames(cgb_shares)))

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_migrants, aes(destination, pct, fill = origin)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = cgb_bold("EU-28")) +
  ## Seven colors, gray last, for "other".
  scale_fill_manual(values = economist_pal()(7)) +
  labs(
    title = "Movers and shakers",
    subtitle = "Intra-European* migrants living elsewhere\n2014, % of total by destination country",
    caption = "*Including EFTA\nSource: European Commission",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: seven classic colors with "Other" last in the key, not named in the panel; and gridlines in the gaps
between bars, where 2017 has none. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#color-overrides-1))

Here each side of the answers takes a color family, blues and reds, with gray for "not sure", like the blue-and-red
set above.
A second measure goes in a column of boxes beside the bars, labeled by a box at its foot. Box blob heads like these
are on `r cgb_of("bar_column_stacked.blob_shape.box", "stacked panels")` (see [Blob heads](#blob-heads)):
`r cite("bar_column_stacked.blob_shape.box", k = 2)`.

```{r cg-bars-trumps-troops, econ_height = 249}
cgb_answers <- c("Enthusiastic", "Satisfied", "Dissatisfied", "Upset", "Not sure")
cgb_troops <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "White men\nno college", "White women\nno college", "White men\ncollege educated",
    "Non-white men\ncollege educated", "White women\ncollege educated", "Non-white men\nno college",
    "Non-white women\ncollege educated", "Non-white women\nno college"
  ),
  share = c(22, 24, 16, 3, 17, 6, 4, 7)
)
cgb_troops$name <- factor(cgb_troops$name, levels = rev(cgb_troops$name))
cgb_pct <- rbind(
  c(29, 24, 14, 31, 2), c(25, 19, 13, 40, 3), c(18, 17, 17, 47, 1), c(18, 12, 11, 51, 8),
  c(13, 15, 14, 57, 1), c(11, 12, 19, 52, 6), c(4, 9, 15, 70, 2), c(5, 7, 17, 67, 4)
)
cgb_feel <- data.frame(
  name = rep(cgb_troops$name, times = length(cgb_answers)),
  answer = factor(rep(cgb_answers, each = nrow(cgb_troops)), levels = cgb_answers),
  pct = c(cgb_pct)
)

cgb_p <- ggplot(cgb_feel, aes(name, pct, fill = answer)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  ## The blob heads: white boxes with a thin dark outline, in a column right of the bars.
  geom_label(
    data = cgb_troops, aes(name, 116, label = share), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "white", label.r = unit(0, "pt"),
    linewidth = lw(0.4), size = classic_size / .pt, label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")
  ) +
  ## The column's heading, in a box of its own under the last row.
  annotate(
    "label", x = 0.45, y = 124, label = "% of total\nvoters, 2012", fill = "white", label.r = unit(0, "pt"),
    linewidth = lw(0.4), size = classic_size * 0.9 / .pt, lineheight = 0.9, vjust = 1, hjust = 1,
    label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "right", limits = c(0, 124), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(1.2, 0.5))) +
  ## Blues for the content, reds for the discontent, gray for "not sure".
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(fg[c("dark blue", "blue", "pink", "dark red", "gray")])) +
  labs(
    title = "Trump's troops",
    subtitle = "How do you feel about Donald Trump as\nthe 2016 Republican nominee\nfor president?*",
    caption = "*5,773 registered voters surveyed\nJune 4th to July 9th 2016\nSources: YouGov; CCES; The Economist",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  cgb_bars_theme() +
  ## Keys a little closer than the theme's, so the three columns of the key end inside the panel's width.
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.9), lineheight = 0.85),
    legend.key.spacing.x = unit(classic_size * 0.6, "pt")
  ) +
  ## Down the columns: the content first, then the discontent.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE))

economist_chart(cgb_p)
```

Against 2017: outlined white boxes, not gray squares sized by value; row names in one weight; and the key under the
subtitle. ([2017 version](economist-2017-styleguide.html#color-overrides-1))
